defect: AUTONOMY_QUEUE_EXISTS_BUT_NO_CONTINUOUS_WORKER. The orchestrator advances only on push-to-coordination-paths, workflow_dispatch and repository_dispatch. That is a CHAIN, not a loop: every link is started by the previous one and no timer anywhere re-enters it. Six scheduled workflows exist (nfl-capture, nfl-availability, nfl-product-board, nfl-status, nfl-t90, nfl-capture-liveness) and NONE starts the agent loop, so any broken link stops autonomy permanently and silently. Three conditions compound it: (1) all 7 orchestrator runs died in PRE-FLIGHT at test_orchestrator::test_z_the_engineering_workflow_is_narrow_and_guarded (FileNotFoundError .github/workflows/claude-engineering.yml) -> SUITE FAIL -> exit 1, before any worker was reached; (2) AUTOMATION_POLICY.json is disarmed (autonomous_operation_enabled=false, execution_mode=MOCK); (3) the OIDC/claude-code-action path cited as the original blocker NO LONGER EXISTS -- commit 5231781 removed every claude-code-action and id-token reference, and the orchestrator now authenticates with ANTHROPIC/OPENAI/PERPLEXITY_API_KEY over urllib. The reported provider-auth failure is therefore NOT still present; it was replaced, and the live blocker sits upstream of auth entirely.

defect: WORKER_CONTAINMENT_BOUNDARY_NOT_ENFORCED. enforce_protected_paths was correct and PROTECTED_PATHS was correct, but changed_paths() handed the check a corrupted path, and a corrupted path matches no prefix, so EVERY protected path was allowed. git status --porcelain is fixed-width (two status columns then a space); _git() strips its whole output; an UNSTAGED modification has a space in column one; stripping ate it and ln[3:] then ate the first character of the path: ".github/workflows/x.yml" -> "github/workflows/x.yml", "coordination/AUTOMATION_POLICY.json" -> "oordination/AUTOMATION_POLICY.json". Measured on a real MOCK pass: all six protected paths NOT CAUGHT, including AUTOMATION_POLICY.json, which holds the two flags authorizing paid execution, and .github/workflows/, which contains the dispatcher the docs call the trust boundary of the whole autonomous system. A worker could therefore have edited the files that define what a worker may do, including arming LIVE. Deletion of a protected file was equally uncaught.
impact: The exposure was the DESIGNED mode, not a corner case: the engineering packet instructs the worker "Do not commit. The workflow commits what you leave in the working tree", so worker changes are unstaged by contract. The single arrangement the parser got wrong is the one the system asks for on every task. Mitigating fact: autonomy has been disarmed and no worker has ever executed, so nothing exploited it. This had to be fixed before LIVE could be armed under any circumstances.
next_action: FIXED: changed_paths() now parses `git status --porcelain -z` with no stripping and no fixed offsets, reports both sides of a rename or copy, and raises GIT_STATUS_UNPARSEABLE rather than guessing on an unrecognised record. Reading the code did not find this and could not have -- both halves looked right in isolation. Running the loop found it in one pass.
reproduction: In a clone: append a line to any protected file WITHOUT staging it, then call changed_paths() and enforce_protected_paths(). (2) One acceptance-criteria judgement was emitted where the contract requires one per criterion (7 for ENG-001). (3) The fixture's governance_checks SHADOWED the contract keys, producing a return missing eleven of them. (4) The markers "model_called": false and "protected_paths_touched": false were read as the worker CONFESSING a breach, because validate_result treats ANY false value in that object as a breach report -- so the object may hold positive assertions only. (5) No return.md, which ingest requires separately: 400+ characters carrying every section in ENGINEER_RETURN_SECTIONS. SEPARATELY, a real defect in the shipped path: ingest prefers an on-disk CLAUDE_RETURNS/<task>/result.json over CLAUDE_STRUCTURED with no freshness check, and it commits whatever the worker leaves -- so a RETRY of a task reads the PREVIOUS attempt's return. It fails closed (the stale head_before is caught) but it fails closed forever: every retry re-reads the same stale file and burns the retry budget on a deadlock, blaming the worker.
impact: Stage 5 of the acceptance test -- "result is ingested" -- could not have passed. The loop would have delegated, executed, and then refused its own return on every pass, looking like a governance failure rather than wiring. The stale-result precedence would additionally deadlock any retried task.
next_action: FIXED: the worker reads its authorized base, criteria and governance keys FROM THE CONTRACT AND THE PACKET rather than carrying copies that rot, writes a return.md whose headings derive from ENGINEER_RETURN_SECTIONS, and asserts only in the positive. The pre-flight now clears a previous attempt's result.json when it emits the packet, so anything in the return directory afterwards belongs to this run. Rehearsal now ends ENGINEERING_RETURN_ACCEPTED, ENG-001 ACTIVE -> RETURNED, through the real ingest, real containment check and real commit.
reproduction: Rehearsed in a scratch clone: orchestrator --ignore-switch --max 1 to delegate ENG-001, then mock_worker.py, then the real ingest_engineering_return.py. defect: KICKER_ACTUAL_DK_POINTS_NOT_COMPUTABLE. actuals.NUMERIC pulls fg_made and fg_att and nothing else for a kicker: no xp_made, no xp_att, and no field-goal distance buckets. DK and FanDuel both score kickers 3/4/5 by distance plus 1 per extra point, and score_kicker() without buckets falls back to charging EVERY make at the under-40 rate and every extra point at zero. So a kicker with two field goals, one from 45, and three extra points scores 6 against a true 10. This was hidden behind DEF-060: while grading never enumerated kickers at all, the actual-side gap could not be reached. Fixing the universe exposed it. The PREGAME side is fine -- SL.assemble already reads fgm/fga/xpm/xpa and the distance buckets off the kicking layer, so the projection is exact. The asymmetry is the finding: we can project a kicker precisely and cannot yet score what he did.
impact: Kickers can be projected but not graded, so the learning loop is blind to a whole position and the prospective ledger looks more complete than it is. Grading them from the fields that DO exist would be worse than not grading them: it would put a confident wrong actual into the ledger and attribute the error to the model. Chosen behaviour is therefore to ENUMERATE the kicker and mark his DK points KICKER_ACTUALS_INSUFFICIENT, which makes the gap countable.
next_action: This needs bytes from outside the repository -- the outcome feed must carry xp_made, xp_att and field-goal distance buckets (or per-kick distances from which buckets can be derived). Written into docs/AGENT_OUTBOX.md for the agent that holds network access rather than marked blocked, since it is assigned rather than blocked. Until then the named state stands.
reproduction: grep xp_made nfl/postgame/actuals.py -> absent; NUMERIC at line 46 lists fg_made and fg_att only. nfl/dfs/scoring/draftkings.py:58 score_kicker falls back to RULES['fg_made_under_40'] * fg_made + RULES['xp_made'] * xp_made with xp_made zero. nfl/tests/test_kicker_reaches_every_consumer.py::test_grading_enumerates_kickers_and_refuses_to_invent_their_actuals asserts the gap is still real, so if xp_made ever appears the test says to re-derive this rather than assume it.

defect: NO_PINNED_MODULE_CAN_RUN_A_DIFFERENT_GAME. Of the 35 modules the cross-layer audit reports FIXTURE_PINNED, NOT ONE accepts a game, week or slate argument. Eighteen are runnable entry points (__main__); exactly one imports argparse at all and even that has no game option. So running a different game requires EDITING SOURCE in every case. That is the defect, and it is sharper than '35 modules mention DET_BUF': a runnable script that silently resolves last month's slate is a trap for whoever runs it next, and it will produce a confident artifact for the wrong game. Classified per the owner's five categories: (a) SLATE RESEARCH in a production tree -- 17 modules in nfl/dfs/showdown/ pinned across FOUR one-off slates (DET_BUF_2026W2, IND_KC_SHOWDOWN_2026W2, NYG_LA, NYG_LAR); (b) ONE SPECIFIC GRADING RUN -- 7 modules in nfl/postgame/ pinned to DET_BUF_2026W2, including one named run_week2.py, which is the strongest real parameterisation candidate; (c) FROZEN REFERENCE reads -- dual_board, site_rules, dependence read the frozen artifact deliberately, because the frozen slate is the point of the comparison; (d) SUPERSEDED -- production/board/run_board.py is a one-game runner replaced by tools/refresh_boards.py, which is what the workflow runs; (e) NOT PINS AT ALL -- 2 of the 35 are provenance LABELS, see below.
impact: MITIGATED BUT NOT EXONERATED: a 97-module import closure over the six scripts the scheduled workflows actually run reaches NONE of the pinned input paths. The pinned cohort is manually-invoked tooling, so no scheduled run is producing wrong-game artifacts today. The exposure is a person running one of the 18 and getting a plausible artifact for a slate they did not mean.
next_action: The rule is in place: a hard-coded game path in a production tree must be DECLARED with a reason, and every declaration's 'not reachable from live' half is CHECKED rather than trusted, so a declaration that stops being true fails. Real parameterisation next, in priority order: nfl/postgame/ first, because grading a second slate is work we actually need -- and per the owner, each repaired module must be exercised on TWO different games so a fake parameterisation cannot pass by resolving the same fixture underneath. nfl/dfs/showdown/ should move OUT of nfl/dfs/ rather than be parameterised; that is a rename and belongs in its own change.
